title: Grade 10 Science — Ohm's Law, Resistance & Circuits
description: Ohm's Law, series/parallel circuits, resistance, electric power
subject: science

questions.question: Ohm's Law states that, at constant temperature:
options: Current is inversely proportional to voltage
Voltage is proportional to current (V = IR)
questions.explanation: Ohm's Law: V = IR (Voltage = Current × Resistance). At constant temperature, V is directly proportional to I. 'Ohmic' conductors follow this; 'non-Ohmic' (like diodes) do not.

questions.question: If V = 12 V and R = 4 Ω, the current I is:
In a series circuit with resistances R₁ and R₂, the equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + ... In series, current is the same through all resistors; voltage divides. More resistors in series = greater total resistance.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit with resistances R₁ = 4 Ω and R₂ = 6 Ω, the equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: Parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ = 1/4 + 1/6 = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12. R = 12/5 = 2.4 Ω. In parallel, equivalent resistance is LESS than the smallest individual resistance.

questions.question: Household appliances are connected in parallel because:
options: Each appliance gets the same voltage and can be switched on/off independently
Parallel circuits have greater total resistance
questions.explanation: Parallel connection in homes: each appliance gets the full mains voltage (230V), can be controlled independently, and a fault in one doesn't affect others. In series, voltage would be divided and one fault breaks all.

questions.question: The resistance of a wire depends on:
questions.explanation: R = ρL/A. Resistance increases with length L, decreases with cross-sectional area A, and depends on the material's resistivity ρ. Temperature also affects resistance (not in this formula).

questions.question: Electric power is given by the formula:
questions.explanation: Electric power P = VI = I²R = V²/R. P is measured in watts (W). A 60W bulb with 230V supply: I = P/V = 60/230 ≈ 0.26 A.

questions.question: The SI unit of electrical resistance is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω), named after Georg Simon Ohm. 1 Ω = 1 V/A (one ohm is the resistance when 1 volt produces 1 ampere of current).

questions.question: A 40 W bulb runs for 5 hours. The energy consumed in kWh is:
questions.explanation: Energy = Power × Time = 40 W × 5 h = 200 Wh = 0.2 kWh. (1 kWh = 1000 Wh). This is 1 'unit' of electricity = 0.2 units.

questions.question: In a series circuit, if one bulb fuses (burns out), what happens to the other bulbs?
options: They all go out (circuit is broken)
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, there is only ONE path for current. If any element breaks (fuses), the circuit is open and NO current flows — all bulbs go out. This is why Christmas lights in series all go out if one fails.

questions.question: The heating effect of current is used in:
options: Electric heater, toaster, iron, incandescent bulb (filament)
questions.explanation: The heating effect (Joule's Law: H = I²Rt) is used in: electric heater, toaster, electric iron, geyser, incandescent bulb (tungsten filament). Electric motors and generators use the magnetic effect.

questions.question: Three resistors of 3 Ω each are connected in series. The total resistance is:
The same three resistors (3 Ω each) are now connected in parallel. The total resistance is:
questions.explanation: Parallel: 1/R = 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 = 3/3 = 1. R = 1 Ω. For n equal resistors R in parallel: total = R/n = 3/3 = 1 Ω.

questions.question: Nichrome wire is used in electric heaters because:
options: It has very low resistance and melts at low temperatures
It has high resistance and high melting point — resists oxidation at high temperatures
It conducts electricity better than copper
It is cheaper than all other metals
questions.explanation: Nichrome (nickel-chromium alloy) is used in heaters: high electrical resistance (produces lots of heat), high melting point (~1400°C), resistant to oxidation at high temperatures. Silver and copper have low resistance.

questions.question: The commercial unit of electrical energy (1 unit = 1 kWh) equals how many joules?
questions.explanation: 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3,600,000 J = 3.6 × 10⁶ J = 3.6 MJ. This is the energy used by a 1-kilowatt appliance running for 1 hour.
